lit.\u0027¿Qué reduce una cetona pero no un: "What reduces a ketone but not an ester?"
lit.\u0027\u003c/div\u003e\u003cdiv class=\":
"
1 · Oxidation state of the key carbon
"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003e1) El hidruro, nucleó:
"

1) The hydride, a nucleophile, attacks the electrophilic carbon of the C=O; the π electrons move onto the oxygen and an alkoxide forms. 2) The alkoxide is protonated by the solvent (EtOH) or by H₃O⁺ in the final work-up to give the alcohol. The carbon goes from having 1 bond to O (aldehyde: +1) to 1 single C–O bond and 2 C–H (alcohol: −1): it is reduced.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn química orgánica u:
"

In organic chemistry an oxidation increases the number of C–O (or C–N, C–X) bonds or decreases the C–H bonds; a reduction does the opposite. The oxidation state of carbon is obtained by adding −1 for each H, +1 for each bond to O, N or X, and 0 for each C: alkane −3 · 1° alcohol −1 · aldehyde +1 · acid +3 · CO₂ +4. Oxidizing ethanol to ethanal means going from −1 to +1.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa \u003cb\u003equimi:
"

Chemoselectivity makes it possible to reduce one group without touching another: with NaBH₄ a ketone is reduced in the presence of an ester, but with LiAlH₄ both are reduced. In the ester the alkoxy group is lost and two alcohols form (here ethanol + ethanol). Look at the substrate–reagent matrix in “Graphs”.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa oxidación elimina:
"

Oxidation removes the H of the carbinol carbon. A secondary alcohol becomes a ketone (with PCC or Jones; the ketone is not oxidized further). A tertiary alcohol has no H on that carbon and is not oxidized under these conditions. This difference makes it possible to distinguish the three classes of alcohols with the Jones reagent.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa reducción de un gr:
"

Reducing a carbonyl group to an alcohol delivers H⁻ (hydride) to the carbon and H⁺ to the oxygen. Aldehyde → 1° alcohol; ketone → 2° alcohol. NaBH₄ is a mild, selective hydride; LiAlH₄ is much more reactive and also reduces acids and esters (to 1° alcohol), but reacts violently with water.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn alcohol primario s:
"

A primary alcohol is oxidized in two stages: alcohol → aldehyde → acid. With PCC (anhydrous) the reaction stops at the aldehyde. With Jones (aqueous CrO₃/H₂SO₄) the aldehyde is hydrated to the gem-diol and immediately oxidized to the carboxylic acid. In both cases Cr(VI) (orange) is reduced to Cr(III) (green).

"
